name: The AI Readiness gap: Where infrastructure teams are getting AI wrong

2. A behavioral framework for assessing your own AI readiness across five dimensions: AI integration depth, governance maturity, automation coverage, risk exposure, and platform readiness.
3. What Pioneer organizations did differently before AI arrived, why that discipline is now the single biggest predictor of production stability, and the specific steps still available to close the gap before agentic AI removes the margin for error.

name: The cost benefits of modernizing your VM fleet (that no one talks about)
description:
VM modernization involves more financial complexity than what shows up on a standard cloud bill. Most engineers evaluate VMs on on-demand hourly rate, missing private pricing, discount eligibility, and commitment impact. This session gives platform engineers, DevOps, infrastructure teams a practical framework for the cost decisions around VM modernization, including free access to the ProsperOps Price Comparison Tool for Google Cloud.

VM modernization requires decisions most engineers aren’t making. On-demand rate is only part of the picture. Private pricing, discount eligibility on the new VM series, and the impact on your existing commitments all affect whether a migration saves money. The financial levers differ by cloud: Azure has VM expiration deadlines that limit long-term discount options; Google Cloud’s newer 4th gen VMs offer better price-performance without official retirements.

**Andrew DeLave, Senior FinOps Specialist at ProsperOps, **will walk through the financial dimensions of VM modernization in the cloud, including how commitment timing shapes your options and how to measure total outcome.

Outcomes like:

1\. **A framework for evaluating the full financial cost of a VM migration**, including private pricing, discount eligibility, and cost avoided, not just on-demand hourly rate
2\. **A strategy for timing VM transitions against your existing commitments** to minimize unused coverage and avoid locking in to the wrong infrastructure
3\. **Total modernization outcome metrics, including ESR (Effective Savings Rate) and ECOR (Effective Cost Optimization Rate)** before and after migration.

Speaker: Andrew DeLave
Senior FinOps Specialist @ ProsperOps
Andrew DeLave is a Senior FinOps Specialist at ProsperOps with expertise in cloud rate optimization. He works directly with customers on commitment strategy, VM modernization, and measuring cost efficiency outcomes.

What does a roller coaster have in common with a refinery? More than you'd think. This talk applies bowtie analysis — a proven process safety methodology — to theme park ride control systems, showing how OT cybersecurity and functional safety can be quantified together in a single framework.

Theme park ride control systems occupy a rare and underappreciated position in the OT cybersecurity landscape: they are life-safety-critical and continuously networked. While the integrated system is unique to each installation, the components themselves are an integration of commercial IT and OT products, often managed by teams whose primary expertise is mechanical and electrical engineering, not cybersecurity. As cyber threats targeting industrial control systems grow more sophisticated, the theme park industry needs analytical frameworks that speak both languages: the language of functional safety and the language of cyber risk. Bowtie analysis does exactly that.

John will examine managing the risks in these ubiquitous systems using bowtie analysis, which is a visual risk methodology with deep roots in the process safety world, refineries, chemical plants, offshore platforms, where it has been used for decades to map threat and cause pathways to a top event, and consequence pathways from the top event to harm.

This talk is for everyone dealing with ICS/OT cybersecurity risks and their management.

name: Search Is a Content Problem
description:
Search Is a Content Problem: How Metadata, IA, and Governance Shape Discoverability

**About the talk:**

If you've heard users say they feel that your "search is broken" or that "they can't find anything", they're often pointing to a content problem. Search depends on clear titles, useful metadata, and strong content structure. When those pieces are weak, search results can't help your users. In this session, we’ll look at how to find and fix these problems. Lucy will share how audits, metadata reviews, and simple content changes can improve what users see in search. We’ll also look at how to prevent the same problems from coming back by setting clear content rules and standards.

**This will be a hands-on session in Mural.** You are invited to listen and participate at the level you're comfortable with.

**About Lucy:**
Lucy is a Senior Digital Strategist focused on making digital content easier to navigate and use. Her work has included just about every sort of of content strategy task. From complex site audits, microcopy writing, and content modeling. All the way to engaging stakeholders directly to promote better user experiences. She has over two decades of experience in human-centered design, which has served her well in all of her work. She focuses on building relationships with clients to build trust. Which helps bring empathy for all users into the room when decisions get made.
